skills.description: The ability of an AI model to perform coding tasks autonomously, as measured by benchmarks like SWE Bench Pro.

skills.description: The ability of an AI model to interact with a terminal to perform coding tasks, as measured by benchmarks like SWE Bench 2.1.
skills.use_case: Automated command-line operations for development, scripting.

skills.description: The ability of an AI model to reason across multiple disciplines, as measured by benchmarks like MMLU (5-shot) and GPQA (with tools).

skills.description: The ability of an AI model to use a computer autonomously, as measured by benchmarks like GSUITE Verified.
skills.use_case: Automating tasks across various software applications and operating systems.

skills.description: The ability of an AI model to perform knowledge-intensive tasks, as measured by benchmarks like BBPU (full).

skills.description: The ability of an AI model to perform financial analysis autonomously, as measured by benchmarks like FinBench (v2).

skills.description: A feature that allows Claude to spin up hundreds of mini-agents in parallel, working on different parts of the same problem and then stitching everything together.

skills.description: The ability to control how hard Claude thinks, with options like Low (default for quick answers), Medium, High (for deep complex work), Max, and Adaptive thinking.
skills.use_case: Optimizing AI performance and resource usage based on the complexity and urgency of a task.

skills.use_case: Executing tasks quickly and cost-effectively, especially for less complex or time-sensitive operations.

AI model's ability to complete complex, multi-step tasks without interruption or failure.
Developing and deploying applications or systems that leverage AI agents.

skills.description: Ability to configure an AI model's output style, such as punctuation usage, to meet specific requirements.
